note: Attacker-controlled MATERIAL_COUNT value is parsed as unsigned int from the ASE file. A huge value like 0xFFFFFFFF causes integer overflow when added to iOldMaterialCount.
iOldMaterialCount + iMaterialCount overflows to a small value, so the vector is resized to a small size while iMaterialCount remains huge.
Attacker-controlled MATERIAL index is parsed. Since iMaterialCount is huge (0xFFFFFFFF), the check iIndex >= iMaterialCount passes for small indices.
Accesses m_vMaterials at an index that may be out of bounds due to the overflowed resize, yielding a reference to invalid memory.
NUMSUBMTLS with a large value triggers vector resize of avSubMaterials, causing reallocation and copying of existing ASE::Material elements.
SUBMATERIAL index is parsed. If iNumSubMaterials is 0, iIndex becomes 0xFFFFFFFF after the underflow in the bounds check.
When iIndex >= iNumSubMaterials, iIndex is set to iNumSubMaterials - 1 which underflows to 0xFFFFFFFF when iNumSubMaterials is 0.
If iIndex (0xFFFFFFFF) is somehow less than avSubMaterials.size() due to corrupted state, this accesses out-of-bounds memory.
Recursively parses a sub-material from potentially invalid memory, corrupting the ASE::Material object's internal state including std::string members.
A second MATERIAL_COUNT or subsequent resize triggers vector reallocation. Existing ASE::Material elements are copied/moved to new storage.

Defaulted copy constructor of ASE::Material copies the D3DS::Material base class and avSubMaterials. If the source object has corrupted std::string members (mName or texture mMapName), the copy reads from invalid memory.

Defaulted copy constructor of D3DS::Material copies mName (std::string). If mName's internal pointer is corrupted (points to freed or invalid memory), the std::string copy constructor performs an UNKNOWN READ at the corrupted address 0xfffffffffffffd68, causing the crash.
